mission.title: dapr: allow annotation to specify shutdown pause
mission.description: During pod termination the Dapr sidecar (daprd) can begin shutting down before the application has finished draining in-flight work, because `dapr.io/graceful-shutdown-seconds` only bounds how long daprd waits AFTER shutdown starts. Users needed a way to pause the start of sidecar shutdown itself. Dapr added the `dapr.io/block-shutdown-duration` annotation for this. Requested by 7+ users.

steps.title: Check current dapr deployment
steps.description:
Verify your dapr version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n dapr-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=dapr
helm list -n dapr-system 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working dapr installation.

steps.title: Review dapr configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the existing shutdown-related annotations on your Dapr-enabled workloads:
```bash
kubectl get all -n dapr-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=dapr
kubectl get deployment <your-app> -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.metadata.annotations}' | tr ',' '\n' | grep -E 'dapr.io/(graceful-shutdown-seconds|block-shutdown-duration)'
```
Note that `dapr.io/graceful-shutdown-seconds` only bounds how long daprd waits for in-flight work AFTER its shutdown begins — it does not delay the start of shutdown while the app is still healthy, which is the gap this mission addresses.

steps.title: Add the dapr.io/block-shutdown-duration annotation to the workload
steps.description:
Upgrade to Dapr >=1.13 (the release that shipped this feature, tracked in dapr/dapr#4313 and dapr/dapr#7211), then set the `dapr.io/block-shutdown-duration` annotation on the pod template. It blocks the start of daprd's shutdown until either the app reports unhealthy or the duration elapses — distinct from `dapr.io/graceful-shutdown-seconds`, which caps the drain time once shutdown has begun:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        dapr.io/enabled: "true"
        dapr.io/app-id: "my-app"
        dapr.io/block-shutdown-duration: "30s"
        dapr.io/graceful-shutdown-seconds: "15"
```
Apply it:
```bash
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/my-app
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Delete a pod of the annotated workload and confirm daprd pauses before shutting down:
```bash
kubectl delete pod -l app=my-app --wait=false
kubectl logs -l app=my-app -c daprd --tail=20 | grep -i shutdown
kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
The daprd log should show the shutdown being blocked for up to the configured duration (e.g. 30s) while the app health check still passes, and only then beginning the graceful drain.

resolution.summary: The root cause is that `dapr.io/graceful-shutdown-seconds` only limits how long daprd waits for in-flight work after its shutdown has already begun, so there was no way to delay the start of sidecar shutdown while the application was still draining. Dapr resolved this by adding the `dapr.io/block-shutdown-duration` annotation (disabled by default): it blocks the entire shutdown procedure until either (1) the app reports as unhealthy, or (2) the configured duration elapses. Because the sidecar stays fully functional during the block, the application keeps access to Dapr APIs while it finishes its own drain, after which the normal graceful shutdown (bounded by graceful-shutdown-seconds) proceeds.
